_comment: WATCHDOG session permissions. Watchdog server only -- no motion/gripper/scene rule, so a config mistake that leaked a command server into this session would still prompt before the arm could be moved. The deny list is the session-level half of the independence guarantee: role_context.py notes that role is derived from the environment and get_rendered_task is hosted only on this role's server, so 'neither role has any tool capable of naming the other's file'. That holds at the MCP layer only. A watchdog session with Read can open agents/tasks/fmb_assembly.executor.yaml directly, and one that can spawn a subagent can have it do the reading under its own permissions -- either way the watchdog learns the executor's rendering, which is the one thing the two-file split exists to prevent. The watchdog observes through its MCP tools (get_execution_state, get_events, get_evidence, wait_for_event) and records through record_verdict, all server-side; it needs no filesystem, shell, or network access to do its job.
